headline: A freshly measured lactate threshold of 4:24/km confirms aerobic fitness remains sharp despite a week that deliberately stepped back from high-load work.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The threshold test result is the headline data point this week — a demonstrated 4:24/km at 178 bpm is a concrete fitness marker that sits firmly in the context of your PB progression from 5K through half-marathon. It anchors any interpretation of recent volume movement: the modest week following the 27 June tempo effort is not a signal of regression, it's a normal load-response pattern. The 13+ km recovery run at controlled effort the day after the threshold test is coherent management.

The broader 4-week picture is quietly positive. Volume has grown 13% block-on-block, and the more meaningful signal is that your easy-run HR has dropped noticeably at comparable efforts — that kind of cardiac drift downward at similar paces reflects real aerobic adaptation, not a favourable condition on a single day. Strength consistency has ticked down slightly but remains well within normal variance for a multi-modal athlete in a running-heavy block.

Your 20-week running streak has now matched your previous best. Whether you extend it or not is secondary to the quality of what's been built — but it's worth noting as a marker of structural consistency across the whole period.
watch_items: Track whether easy-run HR continues its downward trend over the next 2–3 sessions, or stabilises — either tells you something about where adaptation currently sits.
The threshold test provides a single reference point; note how it feels to run at or near 4:24/km in upcoming efforts to start building subjective calibration alongside the number.
Strength dropped to 5 sessions this block — worth observing whether the next 4 weeks recover toward 6–7 without competing with the run load that's now growing.
Back-to-back run durability (as on 2 July after 27 June) is relevant to your ultra capacity — notice how recovery quality between those efforts compares as volume continues to build.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 141 km vs 125 km prior block (+13%)
